frameworks.name: Pitch applicability gate (considered vs unconsidered purchase)
frameworks.decision: Whether to build a full pitch storyboard, a compressed 'teach how to buy' version, or none
evidence_required: number of people in the decision
prerequisites: a sales conversation exists (call, demo, consult, site visit) or a long-form page/video the buyer studies

branches.if: unconsidered purchase: low price, immediate, single buyer, impulse or habitual (consumer goods, low-ticket apps)
branches.then: do not build a pitch storyboard; use offer clarity, landing-page hero and proof (landing-pages skill)

branches.if: local service booked by phone for an urgent or low-ticket job
branches.then: no storyboard; answer price, availability and next step fast (sales-follow-up)

branches.if: high-ticket considered local or consumer job (renovation, roofing, legal, financial planning)
branches.then: compressed guide: 2-3 criteria that actually matter, when the cheaper option is fine, narrowed options, honest recommendation, one next step

branches.if: considered B2B purchase with several credible alternatives
branches.then: full 8-step storyboard

branches.if: the only real competitor is the status quo or the landscape is very limited
branches.then: compressed setup (Gearset-style): insight then perfect world; problem/solution can suffice

branches.if: buyer is expert and the status quo is near-identical to the product
branches.then: a product walkthrough may work; still lead with differentiators

steps: Read salesMotion, salesCycle, aov, complexity and customerType
Classify considered vs unconsidered
Pick full, compressed or none
Record the reason so the owner can override
exceptions_failure_modes: Applying B2B storyboard to a $15 consumer product adds friction
Treating a high-stakes consumer purchase as unconsidered (toilet case shows guidance helps)
Label-based gating: some B2C purchases are considered and some B2B are not

requirements.labor: owner or rep time for calls
requirements.capability: someone who can hold a guided conversation

metrics: share of sales conversations ending with an agreed next step
guardrails: The gate is a strategic preference, not a hard block; owner can override
stop_review: Revisit when price, sales motion or buyer group changes
alternatives: No sales conversation at all: carry insight + value themes into the page or a buyer's guide (K7)
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: Dunford scopes the method to 'any considered purchase' and uses B2B tech throughout; her toilet anecdote shows the guide principle in a consumer considered purchase. The local-service branches are ClimbOS inference, not author text.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: generate a pitch storyboard only when salesMotion is sales_assisted or sales_led, or salesCycle is medium/long, or aov is high; otherwise skip and say why
proposed: for local services, use the compressed 'teach how to choose' form only for high-ticket considered jobs

frameworks.climbos_location: skills/positioning/SKILL.md step 11; shared/acquisition/scoring.ts:16-18 dimensions as inputs

relation_to_existing.note: Positioning skill always writes a pitch and suggests a plumber insight for B2C/local; 11 §1 has a motion ladder. This adds the considered/unconsidered gate from the primary source.

frameworks.disagreements: positioning SKILL.md step 11 and strategy-positioning.md apply the pitch to B2C/local generically; the book scopes it to considered purchases. Decider: the purchase's stakes and decision group, not the business label.

frameworks.name: Positioning prerequisites and positioning-to-pitch mapping
frameworks.decision: Whether positioning is ready to build a pitch on, what is pitched, to whom, and which positioning input feeds each step
evidence_required: documented five positioning components with evidence
who sits in the first call (champion)
prerequisites: positioning canvas from the positioning skill / 03_positioning.md workflow

branches.if: any of alternatives, differentiated value or best-fit is undefined or unevidenced
branches.then: repair positioning first; pitch output is labelled draft

branches.if: pre-launch or only a few paying customers
branches.then: build the pitch on a 'positioning thesis', kept loose; tighten after paying customers validate

branches.if: multi-product company
branches.then: decide whether the first call pitches the company (then discovery picks products) or one lead product

branches.if: several stakeholders
branches.then: tune to the champion; prepare material the champion can use with IT, users, legal, economic buyer

branches.if: a competitor never appears on shortlists
branches.then: leave it out of the pitch; track it in strategy only

steps: Check each component exists with evidence
Map: insight <- value + best-fit; alternatives <- alternatives; perfect world <- value; introduction <- category; value step <- value + capabilities; proof <- proof
Take objections and ask from sales history
Name the audience (champion) and the pitched unit
Set review: about twice a year and on market change
exceptions_failure_modes: Pitch built from features because positioning was skipped
Pitching to the economic buyer in call one when the champion screens vendors
Treating thesis positioning as validated

requirements.labor: owner plus anyone who talks to customers
requirements.measurement: list of last deals and who was shortlisted

metrics: share of deals where pitched alternatives matched the real shortlist
guardrails: No pitch claim without a positioning component behind it
stop_review: Positioning review triggers (new shortlisted competitor, capability change, buyer change) also invalidate the pitch version
alternatives: No customers yet: thesis positioning plus broad exposure (BK03 exploration mode)
frameworks.interpretation: Repeat vs new: the five components, their order, the so-what chain, shortlist-only competitors, thesis positioning and periodic review repeat Obviously Awesome (BK03). New: the explicit mapping to pitch steps, champion-first audience, multi-product decision, objections/ask sourced from sales experience. Note the book lists five components and drops OA's optional trend; the pitch's Insight step takes the framing role a trend might have played. Value themes: 'three or fewer' here vs BK03 notes '1-4'.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: a pitch artifact must reference a PositioningVersion id; if that version changes, the pitch is marked stale
proposed: cap value themes at three in pitch and messaging outputs

relation_to_existing.note: Mostly duplicates BK03 on components; add only the mapping table and champion/multi-product rules as a v2 section of 03_positioning.md, citing BK14 locators. 03_positioning.md already proposes PositioningVersion; extend it with a pitchVersion link.

frameworks.disagreements: BK03 says don't make a positioning statement the primary output; positioning SKILL.md step 9 and specs.ts:53 still centre a positioningStatement. Sales Pitch is consistent with BK03: the usable output is the story, not a statement. Decider: keep the statement as an internal summary only.

frameworks.name: The setup: Insight, Alternatives as approaches, Perfect World agreement gate
frameworks.decision: How to open a sales conversation so the market frame points to the business's differentiated value, and whether the prospect is a fit
evidence_required: industry research only if the insight needs backing

branches.if: draft insight is a market trend or generic problem every rival solves
branches.then: reject; derive the insight backwards from the differentiated value (what must the buyer believe for this value to matter?)

branches.if: prospect has likely seen a competitor, or it appears in nearly every deal
branches.then: name it; otherwise describe the approach group without names

branches.if: rival would categorise itself differently
branches.then: allowed if objectively defensible; never false

branches.if: prospect disagrees at Perfect World
branches.then: treat as likely self-disqualification; move to a graceful exit or clarify, don't push

branches.if: prospect agrees
branches.then: move quickly to the follow-through

branches.if: limited landscape
branches.then: skip explicit pros/cons and go insight -> perfect world

steps: Write one insight from value + best-fit (one slide, 1-2 minutes)
Group alternatives into 2-5 approaches incl. status quo
For each: pros and cons for this buyer type (few words)
Draft discovery questions: how do you handle it today, how is that working, what else are you looking at
Write perfect-world criteria that combine the good of each approach and avoid the cons; they must map to the value themes
End with an agreement check
exceptions_failure_modes: Trend-as-insight ('more data than ever', 'AI adoption is accelerating')
Lecture instead of discovery
Setup runs long and value gets squeezed
Introducing new options the buyer then goes away to research
Bad-mouthing or false claims about rivals

requirements.measurement: call notes on where prospects agreed/disagreed

metrics: share of calls where perfect-world criteria were agreed
share of disagreements that were bad-fit on review
guardrails: Every claim about an alternative needs evidence (review, doc, demo, owner-verified)
No invented research to back the insight
stop_review: Prospects repeatedly don't recognise their situation in the approaches: rewrite alternatives
Many good-fit prospects disagree at perfect world: positioning problem, go back to K2
alternatives: No live calls: put insight + approaches on a long-form page or buyer's guide (K7)
frameworks.interpretation: New vs Obviously Awesome: OA (ch13 per BK03) sketched a sales story order; Sales Pitch adds insight-from-value, approach grouping, discovery inside Alternatives, the agreement gate and timing. The agreement gate is the most useful decision rule: it turns the pitch into a fit test.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: flag an insight that would read the same for the top competitor (swap test) or matches a generic-trend pattern
proposed: claims about a named competitor's limits require cited evidence, as for any comparative claim
proposed: perfect-world criteria must each map to a value theme; unmapped criteria are dropped
proposed: target setup at or under about a fifth of first-call time; warn above

frameworks.climbos_location: skills/positioning/SKILL.md step 11; skills/landing-pages/SKILL.md step 4 (B2B order); shared/agents/specs.ts:47-55 (alternatives schema)

relation_to_existing.note: Existing skills already list insight -> alternatives -> perfect world but define insight as 'what's changed' / 'what changed', which the book names as a common mistake. Version both lines.

frameworks.disagreements: 1) landing-pages step 4 and positioning step 11 frame insight as a change/trend; Dunford says trend-led openers can't differentiate. 2) strategy-positioning.md lists Raskin's 'name a shift' narrative for pitch decks; Dunford says vision narratives fit investors and give buyers reasons to delay. Decider: present-tense purchase with a shortlist -> Dunford; investor or category-creation content -> shift narrative acceptable. 3) 11 §3 SPIN discovery is buyer-led; Dunford adds seller teaching. Compatible: ask and teach.

frameworks.name: The follow-through: Introduction, value-themed demo, matched proof, unspoken objections, easy ask
frameworks.decision: How to show the product, prove it, pre-empt hesitation and choose the next step
evidence_required: value themes with the features behind each
proof inventory tagged by industry, role, starting status quo
common unspoken objections from lost/stalled deals
prerequisites: confirmed facts for timelines, certifications, integrations

branches.if: multi-product / platform / infrastructure product
branches.then: introduce with family, platform or 'marketecture' diagram; mark optional add-ons and what is replaced vs connected

branches.if: product demos well
branches.then: demo grouped by value theme, slide before and after

branches.if: little to show (infrastructure) or highly customised
branches.then: slides or example implementation; label what is not in the base product; custom demo becomes the ask

branches.if: capability is required by everyone (security cert, ERP integration)
branches.then: not a value theme; cover it in Objections

branches.if: a common objection has no good answer
branches.then: don't raise it unprompted; log it as a product/offer priority for the owner

branches.if: prospect is a poor fit
branches.then: the ask is a clear, kind exit

steps: One-line category introduction
Up to three value themes, each: claim, features that deliver it, demo or slide
Proof per theme matched to the prospect
Optional: 1-3 unspoken objections with specific answers (deployment time, training, modular start)
One ask that is easy to say yes to, plus who must be involved
exceptions_failure_modes: Feature walkthrough
Same case study for every prospect
'Call us with questions' as the ask
Demo implies custom work is standard
Proactive objection the business can't answer
metrics: share of first calls with an agreed next step
share of bad-fit prospects exiting at call one rather than later
guardrails: Deployment times, certifications and customer names only from confirmed facts
Your own claim is not proof
stop_review: If next-step agreement stays low after the test period, check the ask's complexity before the story
alternatives: No proof yet: demo the mechanism, offer a pilot as the ask, mark proof as [NEEDS FACT]
frameworks.interpretation: Mostly new relative to Obviously Awesome. The table-stakes-to-objections rule and 'don't raise what you can't answer' are practical additions not present in existing skills.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: a value theme that every shortlisted alternative also delivers is moved to objections or parity notes
proposed: every pitch output ends with exactly one primary next step
proposed: certifications and deployment-time statements in pitches pass the existing claim lint

relation_to_existing.note: sales-follow-up already has proof-backed objections and a single specific ask; add proactive unspoken objections and the unanswerable-objection rule. Positioning step 11 omits Introduction and Objections; add them.

frameworks.disagreements: 11 §5 says the demo should show the customer's priority task, tied to discovery; Dunford says the first-call demo shows your best value regardless of request and customisation waits for call two. Decider: if the buyer is a first-time buyer unsure of criteria -> Dunford; if the buyer arrives with explicit tested requirements (RFP, prior trial) -> tailor, while still covering differentiators.

frameworks.name: Pitch test, rollout and upkeep (founder-led adaptation)
frameworks.decision: When a new pitch is good enough to adopt, and how to keep it from drifting
evidence_required: number of qualified first calls per week
call notes or recordings with consent
prerequisites: K3/K4 storyboard turned into deck, demo, script

branches.if: team has reps
branches.then: one respected rep tests on real qualified prospects; builders listen and debrief each call

branches.if: founder-led sales (usual ClimbOS case)
branches.then: owner is the tester; ClimbOS supplies the debrief questions and records the answers

branches.if: tester wants no more changes and prefers the new pitch
branches.then: pass: roll out

branches.if: tester has used it several times, stopped iterating, still prefers old
branches.then: fail: check sales involvement, then positioning

branches.if: call volume too low for a statistical comparison
branches.then: use the qualitative pass/fail plus leading indicators, labelled observational

steps: Pick tester
Run on real qualified calls
After each call: where lost, where excited, what was confusing
Allow wording and small objection fixes only; don't change the core mid-test
Decide pass/fail
Roll out: recorded pitch, practice, check before live calls
Name an owner; recheck on positioning change; recertify periodically
exceptions_failure_modes: Rolling out to everyone at once
Rewriting the core mid-test
Calling a winner from a handful of calls on close rate
Pitch drift after rollout
Tester bias toward the familiar old pitch (author treats preference despite this bias as strong signal)

requirements.labor: listening and debrief time per call
requirements.capability: consent to record calls if recording

metrics: leading: share of qualified calls progressing to next step
share of bad-fit leads exiting early
guardrails: No close-rate 'win' claims without adequate sample (decisions.ts sampleSize)
alternatives: No calls yet: test the insight and perfect-world criteria with 5 customer interviews (PB-interviews)
frameworks.interpretation: New relative to BK03 and the library. The author's pass test is subjective; ClimbOS should keep it but pair it with logged leading indicators and refuse statistical claims at low volume.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: when sampleSize weeks exceed 12 at the owner's call volume, present the pitch test as a qualitative pilot, not an A/B test
proposed: each pitch test logs per-call debrief answers and next-step outcome

frameworks.climbos_location: skills/experiment-design/SKILL.md; shared/analysis/decisions.ts:152 sampleSize; new PB candidate 'PB-pitch-pilot'

relation_to_existing.note: No existing pitch-test guidance. Reuses existing sample-size calculator to choose qualitative vs quantitative reading.

frameworks.disagreements: Experimentation guidance prefers measured comparisons; Dunford accepts expert judgement for long cycles. Decider: computed sample size vs call volume.

frameworks.name: 'Do nothing' as the main competitor in considered sales
frameworks.decision: What a stalled or lost pipeline is losing to, and what the pitch must compete against
evidence_required: closed opportunities coded won / lost-to-competitor / no decision / disqualified
prerequisites: a record of recent deals (even a short list from the owner)

branches.if: no-decision share is high
branches.then: work on confidence: clearer criteria (perfect world), proof, deployment-risk answers, smaller first step; not competitor attacks

branches.if: losses mostly to one rival
branches.then: name that rival in alternatives and sharpen differentiated value against it

branches.if: pitch introduces options the buyer hadn't considered
branches.then: remove them; new options delay decisions

branches.if: few deals (under ~10)
branches.then: treat shares as directional; gather loss reasons

steps: Code each closed deal
Compute no-decision share and decided win rate
Name the status quo alternative explicitly
Add a case for change to insight and objections
exceptions_failure_modes: Reading no decision as 'they like their current tool'
Pitching the future vision so buyers wait
Treating the cited 40-60% as this business's benchmark
guardrails: Reported 40-60% is a cited, dated B2B figure, not a reference range for diagnosis (base-rates.md rule)
alternatives: No deal history: ask the owner for the last 5 that didn't buy and why
frameworks.interpretation: Partly a repeat: 11 §4 and positioning SKILL already include doing nothing and delay as alternatives; voc-research has the habit force. New: no decision is a vote against change driven by fear, and vendors should avoid adding options. Code gap: diagnosis has no sales-stage fields.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: add an optional deal-outcome breakdown to owner inputs; compute no-decision share deterministically
proposed: never use the book's 40-60% as a reference range in diagnosis

relation_to_existing.note: Duplicates status-quo-as-alternative; extends with no-decision diagnosis and 'don't add options'.

frameworks.disagreements: None material. Raskin/vision narratives in strategy-positioning.md risk the delay Dunford warns of in sales contexts.

frameworks.name: Reusing the pitch story beyond sales calls
frameworks.decision: Which marketing, website and product assets should carry which parts of the pitch
evidence_required: who uses the product vs who buys it

branches.if: homepage
branches.then: tagline/category + value themes + proof; doesn't need the full story

branches.if: explainer video or long-form B2B page
branches.then: can run most of the arc compressed

branches.if: considered purchase with first-time buyers
branches.then: buyer's guide: insight + approaches -> categorised value/feature checklist saying which buyers need what; doubles as a shopping-intent lead magnet

branches.if: free tier / trial / product-led
branches.then: onboarding, tips and help surface the differentiated value

branches.if: end users and economic buyer differ
branches.then: separate stories; don't put the buyer pitch in the end-user product

branches.if: conference talk, research report, book
branches.then: carry the insight only; no sales pitch on stage

steps: Pick asset
Pick the pitch parts it needs
Keep all assets on one pitch/positioning version
Route claims through the claim lint
Owner approves before publishing
exceptions_failure_modes: Pasting the 8 slides onto the homepage
Buyer's guide that just lists your features
Research content that is a disguised trend piece unconnected to the value
End-user onboarding pitched at the buyer

requirements.measurement: guide downloads that become calls; onboarding reaching first value

metrics: activation to first value for product-led onboarding
guardrails: Buyer's guide comparisons follow the same evidence rule as the pitch
Marketing consent for guide leads before nurture
stop_review: Positioning version change invalidates all derived assets
alternatives: No video budget: long-form page section with the same order
No sales team: the buyer's guide and page do the teaching
frameworks.interpretation: Partly versions existing guidance: landing-pages step 4 already maps the sales-narrative order onto B2B pages; Dunford says homepages need not follow it, while explainers and buyer's guides can. Lead-magnets has a local 'questions to ask before you hire' checklist, a buyer's-guide analogue.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: homepage briefs use category + up to 3 value themes + proof; full storyboard order only for long-form pages, explainers and buyer's guides
proposed: add 'buyer's guide' as a lead-magnet type for considered B2B purchases, built from insight + approaches

frameworks.climbos_location: skills/landing-pages/SKILL.md step 4; skills/lead-magnets/SKILL.md table; skills/lifecycle-email/SKILL.md onboarding

relation_to_existing.note: 03_positioning.md already says keep sales, page and onboarding on one positioning version; BK14 adds which pitch parts each asset uses.

frameworks.disagreements: lead-magnets 'never propose a trend report' vs Dunford's insight-led research: compatible if research tests the insight with real data rather than restating trends. Decider: does the research connect to the differentiated value?

skill_proposals.change: Version step 11 (pitch narrative): (a) gate by purchase type (K1); (b) full order insight -> alternatives (approaches, pros/cons, discovery questions) -> perfect world + agreement check -> introduction (category) -> up to 3 value themes -> proof -> optional unspoken objections -> one ask; (c) replace 'what's changed' with an insight derived from the differentiated value; (d) remove the plumber example or mark it as the compressed local form for high-ticket jobs only.
skill_proposals.why: Current step omits Introduction, Objections and the agreement gate, and defines insight as a trend, which the book lists as a common mistake.

skill_proposals.change: Step 4 B2B order: change 'insight (what changed)' to 'insight that points to the differentiated value'; state that homepages lead with category + value themes and need not follow the story; use the full order for long-form B2B pages and explainers.
skill_proposals.why: Matches the source; prevents trend-led openers.

skill_proposals.change: Add: proactive answer to the most common unspoken worry (switching or deployment effort, with real timelines) in the day-0 summary for considered jobs; never raise an objection the business can't answer, flag it to the owner instead; for high-ticket local quotes, a 'how to choose' line (2-3 criteria, when cheaper is fine).
skill_proposals.why: Fear of change drives no decision; toilet-store guide pattern.

skill_proposals.change: Add buyer's guide for considered B2B purchases: insight + approaches -> categorised criteria checklist saying who needs what; mark downloads as active-shopping signals.
Add a v2 section 'From position to pitch' with the mapping table, champion-first audience, applicability gate and pitch test; cite BK14 locators. Don't duplicate the five components.
skill_proposals.why: Version rather than duplicate; the guide's final paragraph already says to turn the position into a sales explanation.

skill_proposals.change: §3: add two-way teaching discovery for first-time buyers. §5: note first-call demo shows differentiated value; tailored demo in call two unless buyer arrives with tested requirements.
skill_proposals.why: Resolves the tension with Dunford explicitly.

skill_proposals.change: Replace the secondary-summary citation (Product Andrew, Lenny's) for Sales Pitch with BK14 locators; fix the 'Built for B2B; adapt insight for B2C/local' line to the considered-purchase scope.
